themes_detail.label: Taxi Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Taxi complaints have spiked to 5 complaints this week versus a weekly average of 0.8 over the prior 8 weeks—a 567% increase—suggesting an emerging transportation service issue in Midtown that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 5 taxi complaints filed this week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.13)
Statistically significant spike (z-score 5.13 indicates high confidence deviation from baseline)
Complements broader transit complaints: 402 taxi complaints and 432 for-hire vehicle complaints over 90 days in Midtown
reporting_angles: Interview taxi drivers and riders to identify specific grievances: service quality, pricing, availability, or safety issues
Cross-reference 311 data with TLC complaints to determine if pattern is coordinated or fragmented

themes_detail.label: LinkNYC Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: LinkNYC complaints exploded to 3 complaints two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike—indicating potential widespread outages or malfunction of the city's public Wi-Fi and service kiosks across Midtown.
evidence: 3 LinkNYC complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)
Spike represents a 2300% deviation from 8-week baseline—most extreme anomaly in dataset
LinkNYC kiosks are high-visibility infrastructure; failures affect tourists, commuters, and residents dependent on free public internet
reporting_angles: Identify which LinkNYC kiosks failed and for how long; assess city repair response times
Interview users about impact: did outages disrupt navigation, communication, or emergency access for vulnerable populations?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints jumped 116% to 65 complaints last week from a 30.1 weekly average—indicating either a city crackdown on street vending or an uptick in vendor disputes affecting Midtown's commercial ecosystem.
evidence: 65 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 30.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.46)
432 total vendor enforcement complaints over 90 days—already a top-5 complaint category
Midtown is dense commercial district where street vendors are economically important; enforcement spike affects workers and food access
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors to determine whether complaints are from enforcement actions, permit denials, or territorial disputes
Investigate whether city shifted enforcement priorities; speak to Parks Enforcement or Community Affairs
Profile vendors affected: food vendors, souvenir sellers, etc. and document impact on livelihoods

themes_detail.label: Missing and Dangling Street Signs
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked dramatically—missing signs up 967% to 4 complaints last week (vs. 0.4 baseline), and dangling signs up 229% to 7 complaints 3 weeks ago—indicating possible infrastructure decay or weather-related damage affecting navigation and safety in Midtown.
evidence: Missing street signs: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49, 967% increase)
Dangling street signs: 7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.84, 229% increase)
Combined signal suggests coordinated infrastructure maintenance failure across signage in district
reporting_angles: Investigate DOT maintenance schedule: are sign repairs backlogged or under-resourced?
Document safety implications: missing directional signs, street names, and hazard warnings affect pedestrians, cyclists, and delivery workers

themes_detail.label: Building Infrastructure and Door/Window Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints spiked 142% to 10 complaints last week from a 4.1 weekly baseline, suggesting emergent building maintenance failures, possible weather damage, or inadequate landlord compliance across residential and commercial properties in Midtown.
evidence: 10 door/window complaints last week vs. 4.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.05, 142% increase)
Complements broader housing and heat/hot water complaints: 552 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days indicate systemic building infrastructure issues
Spike suggests acute trigger—possible weather event, systemic maintenance backlog, or enforcement action
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints cluster in specific buildings or are dispersed; assess landlord compliance patterns
Investigate whether spike is weather-related (recent wind, cold snap) or structural (aging building stock)
